input.summary: A close friend of Sir Bobby Charlton is cycling thousands of miles to raise money for grassroots football
input.evidence_text: The late Sir Bobby Charlton would be "very, very proud" of the work done by community football coaches supported by his charity foundation, one of his close friends has said John Sheils, who sits on the Sir Bobby Charlton Foundation's board, is nearing the end of a charity cycle ride which takes in the stadiums of all 92 clubs in the Premier League and Football League Sheils said he aimed to raise money for children's football across the UK as well as highlight the importance of what Manchester United legend Sir Bobby called "the best toy ever invented" The former CEO of the Manchester United Foundation was speaking on the 60th anniversary of Sir Bobby's England winning the World Cup Sheils, who first met Sir Bobby 47 years ago, spoke warmly of his late friend, who died in 2023 aged 86 Together, they established the Bobby Charlton Soccer Schools which thousands of youngsters attended during school holidays

title: Historic manor house to be restored with lottery cash

input.lead: The Grade II-listed Rock Hall was built in 1807 and has been empty for more than 10 years
input.summary: The Grade II-listed Rock Hall was built in 1807 and has been empty for more than 10 years
input.evidence_text: A derelict house within a country park in Greater Manchester is set to become a visitors centre for a wildlife conservation charity with the help of National Lottery funding The Grade II-listed Rock Hall, inside the Moses Gate Country Park in Farnworth, was built in 1807 and has been empty for more than 10 years Sam Elliott, the head of culture at Bolton Council, said: "Rock Hall has got a lot of heritage and there's a lot of ambition in the restoration project but it does need a lot of work doing to it." "The house would've looked very grand when it was built, surrounded by what would've been an industrial landscape of mills and factories." "We want to tell the story of the Crompton family who built the hall and the tenants who lived in the building during the 19th century," he said Bolton Council has secured a grant of almost £4.5m from The National Lottery Heritage Fund to deliver the Rock Hall Revival project with the Lancashire Wildlife Trust

title: Death of autistic man handcuffed by police under investigation

input.lead: Ricky Swindells, 28, was "in crisis on the floor" when he was restraining by GMP officers
input.summary: Ricky Swindells, 28, was "in crisis on the floor" when he was restraining by GMP officers
input.evidence_text: The death of an autistic man who stopped breathing after being placed in handcuffs "for his own safety" is being investigated by the police watchdog Greater Manchester Police were called to Duchy Road, Salford, on Friday 24 July by the family of 28-year-old Ricky Swindells, who said he was experiencing a mental health crisis The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said it would be investigating the "decision-making" of the officers and the "necessity, proportionality and rationale" for handcuffing Swindells GMP said it had referred itself to the IOPC and was supporting the investigation, and that its officers had acted to try and "de-escalate" the situation The initial results of a post-mortem could not determine the cause of Swindells' death and further forensic work, including toxicology testing, is ongoing The IOPC said it had reviewed body-worn camera footage from the officers involved, which showed them stating he was being restrained "for his own safety"

title: Greenfield villagers say moorland fires getting worse every year

input.lead: Those living in the shadow of the still-raging Dove Stone fire say they feel "hurt" by the lasting damage
input.summary: Those living in the shadow of the still-raging Dove Stone fire say they feel "hurt" by the lasting damage
input.evidence_text: Villagers living in the shadow of a Greater Manchester moorland fire that continues to burn after three weeks say they "feel like they've been hurt" after the treasured landscape went up in flames Firefighters are still tackling the blaze at Dove Stone Reservoir in Saddleworth, which broke out on 11 July after a period of hot weather and low rainfall, before merging with other wildfires For those living in nearby Greenfield, road closures and the near-constant movement of fire engines have become a regular sight Deborah Hill, who works in interior design shop My Secret Boutique, said: "I think it's worrying about what is up there with the animals and wildlife and how long it will take for it to recover." She told the Local Democracy Reporting Service : "The fires are happening every year and they are getting worse every year. This is a bad one because it has gone on for weeks. That is worrying." While things have quietened now, she said: "Every day you generally see about six fire engines going past. You might see at least two police cars. Sirens all the time. It's like being in the city

title: Manchester stabbing: Man, 19, in 'life-threatening' condition

input.lead: Police say a man in his 20s was arrested at Manchester Airport within three hours of the stabbing
input.summary: Police say a man in his 20s was arrested at Manchester Airport within three hours of the stabbing
input.evidence_text: Manchester stabbing: Man, 19, in 'life-threatening' condition - BBC News Image caption, An emergency services helicopter was seen above the scene in Manchester city centre By Ewan Gawne and Jonny Humphries , North West Published 31 July 2026 A teenager has been taken to hospital with life-threatening injuries after he was stabbed in Manchester city centre, police have said. The 19-year-old was found on Church Street in the Northern Quarter after Greater Manchester Police (GMP) were called at about 12:50 BST. Officers had received reports of an "ongoing incident" in the area, said a GMP spokesperson. The force later confirmed that within three hours of the stabbing, a man in his early 20s had been arrested at Manchester Airport on suspicion of wounding with intent. The victim remains in hospital in a stable condition. Det Ch Insp Chris Woodburn said: "Our officers have worked at an incredible pace to piece together what had happened, which has led to us arresting a suspect at the airport. "In any incident of this nature, it is understandable for those who live and work in the area - including members of the public who have come to visit Manchester - to feel apprehensive. "I would like to reassure everyone that there will be an increased police presence in the area as we head into the evening." title: Oldham woman becomes world's first to receive new cancer therapy

input.lead: Tracy Tomlinson was offered the clinical trial for ovarian cancer at The Christie hospital in Manchester
input.summary: Tracy Tomlinson was offered the clinical trial for ovarian cancer at The Christie hospital in Manchester
input.evidence_text: A woman with advanced ovarian cancer has become the first patient in the world to receive a pioneering new therapy Tracy Tomlinson was given the drug at The Christie hospital in Manchester as part of a clinical trial evaluating a new type of treatment for several types of cancer The therapy, known as ZI-MA4-1, will be tested on people with ovarian cancer, lung cancer, sarcomas and head and neck cancer in a trial led by the Christie, and a site at the Royal Marsden in London The 58-year-old, from Chadderton, Oldham, decided almost straight away she was going to go for it, she said, although she admitted it was a "little bit scary" being the first person to have the treatment Many people in the early stage study - which is primarily focused on safety - have few other options for survival Tomlinson has already beaten the odds in staying alive, having undergone surgery and several rounds of chemotherapy since she was diagnosed in 2020

input.evidence_text: The landlady of a legendary city centre pub has died after pulling pints behind the bar for 55 years Nancy Swanick, had run the Peveril of the Peak on Great Bridgewater Street, Manchester, since 1971. Andy Burnham's successor has been named Comments News Ryan Price 23:08, 31 Jul 2026 View Image Ballots are sorted for the second count of votes in the Gr Greater Manchester has a new mayor after a count which lasted all day Polling stations closed at 10pm on Thursday night (30 July) after a long, hot day in the region. The count got underway at 9am this morning (Friday, 31 July), with hundreds gathering inside Co-Op Live to thumb through the voting cards At 2pm this afternoon, the turnout was revealed at just 25.14%. This equated to 538,659 votes being cast from an electorate of 2,142,779 It is the lowest turnout ever for a Greater Manchester mayoral electin. At the 2024 election - in which Andy Burnham was appointed for a third term - the turnout was 32.05pc. It was 28.9% in 2017, and 34.7% in 2021 At 11pm, after the second preference votes were counted, the winner of the election was finally revealed as Labour candidate Bev Craig

It means that despite a first count taking place, no winner can yet be named This is because the election is using the supplementary voting system (SV), which is different to the one traditionally used in general and most local elections This system was used at the mayoral elections in 2017 and 2021, but not in 2024, which used first past the post SV means that voters choose their first and second-choice candidates, rather than just ticking one box Under the system, if any candidate gets more than 50% of the valid first-choice votes, then they will be elected as mayor

input.summary: Greater Manchester Police Death of man detained in Salford investigated by police watchdog Ricky Swindells died last week. An Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) probe is underway
input.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police Death of man detained in Salford investigated by police watchdog Ricky Swindells died last week. An Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) probe is underway. News Todd Fitzgerald Executive editor 17:55, 31 Jul 2026 Upda The death of a man detained in Salford is being investigated by the police watchdog. Ricky Swindells, 28, was dealt with by officers last Friday (July 24) after they attended a property on Duchy Road following a 999 call A report of concern for Mr Swindells' welfare was made, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said. During the call, at around 7.40pm, his family said he was autistic and in 'significant distress' Police handcuffed Mr Swindells to restrain him, the IOPC added. Body worn camera footage shows officers saying that was done for his own safety, the watchdog said Mr Swindells then became unresponsive, the IOPC said, before receiving treatment at the scene. Officers began CPR at 8pm and paramedics arrived seven minutes later, the watchdog added. Officers gave CPR before North West Ambulance Service personnel took over, the IOPC said Mr Swindells was taken to hospital, where he died the next day, Saturday, July 25. Greater Manchester Police said it is supporting the investigation. The force said Mr Swindells was 'restrained by officers responding to a report by family members of a man in crisis'

title: Death of man detained in Salford investigated by police watchdog

input.lead: Greater Manchester Police Death of man detained in Salford investigated by police watchdog Ricky Swindells died last week.
input.summary: Greater Manchester Police Death of man detained in Salford investigated by police watchdog Ricky Swindells died last week. An Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) probe is underway
input.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police Death of man detained in Salford investigated by police watchdog Ricky Swindells died last week. An Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) probe is underway. News Todd Fitzgerald Executive editor 17:55, 31 Jul 2026 Upda The death of a man detained in Salford is being investigated by the police watchdog. Ricky Swindells, 28, was dealt with by officers last Friday (July 24) after they attended a property on Duchy Road following a 999 call A report of concern for Mr Swindells' welfare was made, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said. During the call, at around 7.40pm, his family said he was autistic and in 'significant distress' Police handcuffed Mr Swindells to restrain him, the IOPC added. Body worn camera footage shows officers saying that was done for his own safety, the watchdog said Mr Swindells then became unresponsive, the IOPC said, before receiving treatment at the scene. Officers began CPR at 8pm and paramedics arrived seven minutes later, the watchdog added. input.evidence_text: A decade on, it's one of Altrincham's quiet success stories Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Ed Bright gave up a secure career at one of the world's biggest banks to teach himself to brew beer from scratch. Ten years on, Stubborn Mule Brewery & Tap has become one of Altrincham's most quietly cherished local businesses - and Ed still make When Ed Bright left his job at the BNY Mellon bank in 2015 with nothing but a personal loan, a borrowed shed in Timperley and a pile of brewing books, some may have questioned the wisdom of his decision A decade on, Stubborn Mule is one of Altrincham's quiet success stories - and Ed is still the only one making the beer Appropriately enough, it is a back story built on a stubborn refusal to give up. Ed spent 12 years in banking, working up to a decent middle management level, but by the time Lehman Brothers collapsed in 2008 he was watching colleagues disappear without replacement "It just wasn't doing it for me," he says. With his wife Swan expecting their second child, he made the call. "There was no point getting hung up about sitting behind a desk for the next 10 years. I wanted a challenge."

title: Oldham bucks national trend as more young people choose education and training

input.lead: Oldham has recorded participation rates above both regional and national averages while significantly reducing the number of young people who are not in education, employment or training (NEET)
input.summary: Oldham has recorded participation rates above both regional and national averages while significantly reducing the number of young people who are not in education, employment or training (NEET)
input.evidence_text: Oldham has recorded participation rates above both regional and national averages while significantly reducing the number of young people who are not in education, employment or training (NEET) The latest Department for Education (DfE) Local Authority Participation and NEET figures for the 2025/26 academic year show that 93.2 per cent of Oldham's 16 and 17-year-olds are participating in education and training, an increase of 2.8 percentage points on the previous year. This compares favourably with the North West average of 91.8 per-cent and the England average of 92.2 per-cent. At the same time, Oldham's combined NEET and Not Known (NK) rate has fallen to 4.6%, down 1.1 percentage points from 2024/25. This is significantly lower than both the North West average of 5.5% and the England average of 5.8%. The figures also highlight Oldham's strong performance, in partnership with the charity Positive Steps, in tracking and supporting young people. Positive Steps provides young people with support, careers advice and guidance after school, or between 19 and 25 if they have an Education Healthcare Plan (EHCP), helping them to move into education, training or employment. Only 59 young people out of 7,177 are currently unaccounted for – 0.8 per cent of the borough's young people. This is well below the North West average of 1.3 per cent and the England average of 2.4 per cent. A council spokesperson said: "These figures demonstrate the positive impact of the support available to young people across Oldham. input.evidence_text: A repeat offender who subjected hospital staff to serious abuse and threats has been banned from entering Royal Oldham Hospital except in specific circumstances. On 29 June 2026, Manchester Magistrates’ Court granted a Criminal Behaviour Order (CBO) against Andrew Stonier, 31, after a successful application by Oldham Council's Community Safety Team. The order follows a series of incidents in which the offender made repeated threats towards nurses and hospital staff, including threats to set fire to the hospital. This behaviour caused significant disruption as staff spent hours on end dealing with Stonier, diverting valuable time and resources. As a result of the court order, the offender is prohibited from entering Royal Oldham Hospital until 28 June 2029, except in specific circumstances such as attending a pre-arranged appointment or requiring emergency medical treatment. A breach of the order will result in arrest. The order includes the following restrictions: - Not to enter Royal Oldham Hospital. - Not to enter or attempt to enter any clinical area, ward, department, Accident and Emergency Department, or outpatient facility. - Entry only for a pre-arranged appointment. - When attending an appointment, to arrive within a reasonable timeframe beforehand and leave within 30 minutes of its conclusion. - An exemption applies only where genuine emergency medical treatment is required. An Oldham Council spokesperson said: "This individual's behaviour towards dedicated NHS staff was completely unacceptable. input.evidence_text: Wigan Council is reminding residents to recycle electrical items responsibly this summer due to dangers posed to waste collection crews As temperatures rise and the use of electrical items such as fans, portable chargers, and other rechargeable items increase, the council is urging residents to ensure unwanted electricals are taken to the correct recycling facilities Research from Material Focus has highlighted the growing popularity of low-cost electrical products, often known as ‘FastTech’, which can be easily forgotten, thrown away, or incorrectly disposed of. Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. By taking unwanted electricals to the correct recycling point, residents can help protect our workers, reduce waste, and ensure valuable materials are recovered and reused
